problem: VLMs like CLIP only reason about objects and actions visible in the image, and prior spatial-semantic systems (CLIP-Fields, VLMaps, 3D-LLM) need a full 3D scene model at inference. No method predicts where a natural-language task happens relative to the viewer from a single egocentric image.
motivation: Robots in human environments need to know where people will stand to do tasks, both to navigate to those places and to avoid them. Egocentric datasets such as EgoExo4D give localized frames paired with keystep narrations, which can supervise this spatial affordance.
key_idea: Fine-tune a CLIP image encoder and combine it with a frozen CLIP text encoding in an MLP that predicts a Gaussian over the 3D position where a task occurs, in the query camera frame, trained with a Fréchet-distance loss on rectified positions from other video frames.
insight: Fine-tuning the vision encoder is what gives affordance grounding: multiple-choice accuracy is 63% vs 37% for CLIP-NN, and a frozen-encoder variant gains less. Per-scene adaptation needs little data: one demonstration roughly halves the error on unseen kitchens, and fine-tuning only the head is nearly as good as fine-tuning everything. Generalization to scenes unlike the training kitchens is poor, and the model falls below the baseline there.
method: Problem formulation: given a single egocentric image I and a text task query q, predict a distribution of positions where the task is performed, in the frame of the camera. Poses come from SLAM-localized video.
Image encoder E_V: pretrained CLIP visual encoder, fine-tuned so that it encodes the expected surrounding context and not only the visible content.
Task encoder E_L: frozen CLIP text encoder. GPT-4 rephrasings of each task are used as augmentation during training.
Affordance network A_theta: 4-layer MLP (~1M parameters, layer norm) taking [e_v, e_l] and outputting a 3D mean plus an isotropic ground-plane covariance.

Loss: Fréchet distance between the predicted Gaussian and the target task Gaussian, which is transformed by the pose transform R_x into the query image's frame. Pairs are drawn from different frames of the same video. Only frames with camera velocity below 0.1 m/s are used, and pitch/roll are corrected.
Per-scene fine-tuning: adapt to a new kitchen from one short demonstration (25 epochs, under 30 min), tuning either the head A alone or A plus E_V.
Task obstacles: for a set of tasks, take a region of sigma_bound standard deviations around each predicted Gaussian, discretize it, and take the convex hull as a robot no-go region.

setting.backbone: CLIP (image encoder fine-tuned, text encoder frozen) + 4-layer MLP affordance head
setting.model_size: 1M trainable parameters in the MLP head, plus the CLIP encoder
setting.training_data: EgoExo4D cooking videos: 12 kitchens, 6 activities, ~110 min, 422 task/environment instances; 80/20 task split and 10% held-out consecutive images; GPT-4 rephrasings of tasks
setting.observation: monocular egocentric RGB (Aria) plus a text task query
setting.action_space: none for the model itself; it outputs a 3D task-region Gaussian, which a navigation mesh planner uses to move a simulated Fetch robot
setting.simulator: custom simulator built on images collected with Aria in a training kitchen (Fetch robot model)
setting.privileged: SLAM poses for training supervision only; none at test time (the CLIP-NN baseline uses all localized frames of the scene)

numbers.eval_set_note: held-out tasks and held-out consecutive 10% of images across 12 kitchens seen in training
numbers.extra: trained on the 12 kitchens; the CLIP-NN baseline scores 0.68 ± 0.6 while using all frames of the scene
numbers.evidence: Table 2 Task Region Localization Error, Avg Err: Ours 0.36 ± 0.3 (Baseline 0.68 ± 0.6, Ours E_V frozen 0.42 ± 0.3)

numbers.eval_set_note: 3 unseen kitchens UMN-C, UMN-D, SFU-C, after fine-tuning on one demonstration
numbers.extra: single-demo fine-tune of A and E_V; the base model is 0.55/0.70/1.05

numbers_note: Custom benchmarks on EgoExo4D; no standard navigation benchmark is reported. Figure-only results (localization error box plots) are not captured. Fine-tuning head only (FT A) gives 0.20/0.31/0.45.
results: On seen kitchens with unseen tasks and views, the model reaches 0.36 m average Fréchet error against 0.68 m for the CLIP-NN whole-scene baseline (t(82)=4.683, p<0.001), and 63% vs 37% on 3-way affordance grounding. It is also more stable under rephrasing (0.12 m vs 0.19 m with GPT-4). On unseen kitchens the base model is worse than the baseline, but one demonstration of fine-tuning brings it below the baseline (e.g. 0.18 vs 0.28 m on UMN-C).
limitations: Generalizes only to scenes similar to training, and needs a fine-tuning demonstration for new environments
Only cooking activities in kitchens, and a unimodal Gaussian per task
Navigation is shown only qualitatively in a custom simulator, with no real-robot tests or navigation metrics; human affordances may not map to robots
